so.text: Dots right of the dashed line on an upkeep row are orders the size of a capital request, paid from the operating budget.

blocks.title: Upkeep orders against the capital line

paragraphs.text: The Capital Planning Committee’s definition: **any tangible item costing $20,000 or more with a useful life of three years or longer, or groups of items of the same purpose that together cost at least $20,000.**
Only the cost test can be measured here. A purchase order records what was bought and what was paid, never how long it will last.
Until June 2013 the committee had a form for capital items over $10,000 bought from an operating budget or a grant, Form F. Its minutes record the form being deleted and do not record why.

sub.text: “NEW CABLING PROJECT FOR 911 CO” and “911 COMPLIANCE”, on the school upkeep line
“Districtwide Phone System Upgrade … maintain 911 compliance”, approved 4 September 2024

note.text: Both are the Schools’. The plan is the one the School Committee approved on 4 September 2024; the orders were opened twelve to twenty-one days later.

so.text: The same stated purpose appears on both routes; nothing held says whether the orders covered any of the planned scope.

paragraphs.text: Why any of this work was bought from the upkeep budget rather than taken to capital planning. No document held records the choice.
How long each item will last, the other half of the capital test.

Whether the Town’s Facilities department does the same. Its contracted-services line is described as paying for “smaller projects under the $20,000 threshold”, but its orders are not held: closes: the same MUNIS year-to-date report with journal detail, for department 193.

so.text: Each is capital-sized by cost and was paid from the operating budget, not a capital article.

conclusions.text: 3 one-time jobs paid from the school upkeep budget met the $20,000 capital test: $167,328 in four years.
